questions.scenario: Your best friend is standing for School Captain elections. What is your role?

options.text: Writing catchy slogans and rallying the crowd to vote.
Calculating which class will vote for whom based on past trends.
Managing their Instagram and making them look like a superstar.
Talking privately to the rival team to make a peaceful deal.
Finding out the rival candidate's secret weaknesses and leaking them strategically.
None of these.

questions.scenario: A false rumor is spreading about your group. How do you handle it?

options.text: Counter-attack aggressively and expose the person who started it.
Trace the rumor back to its root to understand their secret motive.
Post a clever, positive story online to clear the group's image gracefully.
Talk calmly to the people spreading it and convince them to stop.
Plant a fake, harmless counter-rumor to confuse everyone and protect the group.
None of these.

questions.scenario: While playing a strategy game (like Clash of Clans or Age of Empires), you focus on...

options.text: Motivating my clan and leading massive, aggressive attacks.
Looking at the whole map and planning long-term resources.
Having the coolest-looking base and a premium clan description.
Forming smart alliances with other clans to avoid unnecessary wars.
Sending small, hidden scout units to perfectly map out the enemy's traps before attacking.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Your team makes a huge mistake in a school project. What is your next move?

options.text: Take charge, pump up the team's energy, and work all night to fix it.
Analyze exactly why the failure happened so it never repeats.
Find a smart way to present it to the teacher so it doesn't look like a failure.
Gently apologize to the teacher and negotiate for one extra day.
Quietly look at what the top-scoring group did and 'borrow' their structure without them knowing.
None of these.

questions.scenario: When you read the news or scroll social media, what catches your attention?

options.text: Who is winning the elections and what promises they are making.
Why two big countries (like US and China) are secretly fighting over trade.
How a celebrity apologized after a massive public controversy.
How two rival companies signed a peaceful partnership deal.
Articles about top-secret spy missions, leaked classified documents, or cyber-attacks.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you were given a 'Mind Control' superpower, how would you use it?

options.text: To make a crowd of 10,000 people believe in my vision instantly.
To see the invisible connections and secrets of world leaders.
To completely erase bad memories or bad images of myself from people's minds.
To calm down angry enemies and make them agree with me peacefully.
To become completely invisible and listen to my enemies' most private conversations.
None of these.

questions.scenario: You have to organize a massive inter-school fest. What is your special duty?

options.text: Hyping up our school's students and keeping the volunteers' energy high.
Planning which rival schools should be kept in separate seating areas to avoid fights.
Handling the official Instagram page to make the fest look premium.
Convincing the strict Principal to allow the DJ party for one extra hour.
Secretly monitoring the crowd in plain clothes to spot any troublemakers before they act.
None of these.

questions.scenario: In a Group Debate or Model UN (MUN), which character are you?

options.text: The Passionate Speaker: Wins the crowd's applause with emotion.
The Researcher: Knows every opponent's secret history and facts.
The Presenter: Drafts the final, beautiful summary for the judges.
The Mediator: Gets two fighting teams to agree on a middle ground.
The Silent Listener: Doesn't speak much but privately manipulates the voting blocks during the break.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Every strategy job has a boring/painful part. Which of these can you tolerate easily?

options.text: Shouting the same speech 50 times in the hot sun to gather people.
Reading 100 pages of boring history and old world maps.
Politely replying to 500 angry comments on a post without losing my temper.
Sitting in a 5-hour long meeting listening to people argue over rules.
Sitting alone in the dark for hours, sorting through messy data to find one hidden clue.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If your team was a chess board, what title fits you the best?

options.text: The Commander (Leads the masses forward).
The Oracle (Sees the big picture from above).
The Illusionist (Manages the image and optics).
The Bridge (Connects enemies and forms alliances).
The Shadow (Moves unseen, gathers information, strikes quietly).
None of these.
